title: Campus test: a consenting volunteer in a real crowd
source: Recorded and combined by the face and privacy teammate; the video is used exactly as delivered.

location.name: Charminar (demo location)
location.note: The clips were filmed on a college campus, not at Charminar. The map pin is a demo location.

enrolment.label: Campus volunteer (consented demo)
enrolment.stored: one averaged embedding, encrypted by the backend; no photos or crops are stored there

held_out_test.what: The face team trained on two clips and tested on a third (IMG_3132), over every face of the volunteer found in it.
notes: Bystanders: the closest of about 215 other faces scored 0.29 against the 0.5 match line.
Clip 4, where he does not appear: nobody matched.
On a crowd frame he was identified at 85% and sent for review; the other 29 faces were pixelated.

stock_sample.note: The InsightFace group-photo clip, where the enrolment photo is cut from the same footage. An easy case, not comparable to real footage.

limits: Confidence is the cosine similarity between face embeddings, shown as a percentage. It is not the probability that the person is right. The match line is 50%.
One volunteer, one campus, four clips. This is a feasibility test, not an accuracy benchmark.
He is matched in only part of the frames where he appears: faces must be clear (detector score 0.6, at least 40 px) before they are checked, and each face is checked at most 3 times.
The face team's own audit at detector score 0.3 found no real face left unblurred, only a shirt and a hand. A face mostly outside the frame, or one too small for the detector, cannot be pixelated.
The recording is 1920×1080, the face pipeline's output. The raw 4K clips show bystanders and are not part of the project files.
Matching depends on the template and on when the checks happen. Re-running the same footage on this backend gave 2 matches at 59–64%, against 60%, 79% and 82% here, so read the numbers as one run.
